basis: Microcephaly and ocular malformations define syndrome; thyroid hypoplasia/hypothyroidism and sensorineural hearing loss each 30–79%; skeletal, renal and vascular anomalies omitted at cap.
Inherited phagocytic-cell dysfunction establishes immune involvement; supplied evidence does not establish common damage to additional organs.
Developmental delay and severe intellectual disability in 5/5; seizures in 3/5. Hypotonia accompanies neurologic disease; visual impairment only 1/5.
Usually infectious inflammation or abscess of fallopian tubes and ovaries; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis.
Cerebral arteriovenous malformation directly affects vessels; supplied evidence does not establish intrinsic brain injury in at least 30%.
Direct traumatic injury causing brain dysfunction.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia is a malignant disorder of blood and marrow lymphoid precursors.
Benign vascular neoplasm arising in the skin; endothelial histology does not establish additional cardiovascular organ damage.
HTLV-1-associated mature T-cell leukemia/lymphoma; direct cutaneous infiltration occurs in roughly 40–60%.
Dyskeratosis congenita features marrow failure and the diagnostic triad of nail dystrophy, skin pigmentation and oral leukoplakia; common additional injury is unestablished for this subtype.
Atherosclerotic disease of cerebral arteries; stroke and vascular cognitive impairment are separate potential sequelae.
Genetically caused bone necrosis defines this umbrella; mechanisms and extraskeletal manifestations vary across subtypes.
Classified as an inherited neurodegenerative disorder; radiation sensitivity and chromosome instability alone do not establish another organ axis.
Congenital familial brachial palsy affects peripheral nerves supplying the arm.
Allergic hypersensitivity to seminal proteins; affected reproductive tissues have no organ axis.
One kidney is developmentally small with a reduced nephron complement.
Trichomonas infection of vulvovaginal reproductive tissues; urinary tract damage is not inherent to this specific concept.
Sixth cranial nerve dysfunction causes impaired eye movement; this does not establish direct injury to ocular tissue.
Ectodermal dysplasia affects sweat glands, skin and hair, with characteristic tooth agenesis; hoarseness alone does not establish airway damage.
Abnormal ciliary-body configuration obstructs ocular aqueous outflow and causes angle-closure glaucoma.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common across the duplication umbrella; other organ anomalies depend on the duplicated segment.
Skeletal dysplasia with brachydactyly and joint restriction; subglottic stenosis in 2/3 and mitral regurgitation in 1/3; skin thickening has no supplied frequency.
Viral infection directly inflames the lung parenchyma.
Renal failure 8/8 and retinal dystrophy 7/8 define the syndrome; developmental delay 3/8 supports neurologic involvement. Hepatic fibrosis 2/8 is below threshold.
Pathologic ocular neovascularization obstructs aqueous outflow and damages vision; diabetes and vascular occlusions are underlying causes, not additional organs damaged by this glaucoma.
